source.title_on_document: VeriForge: Mitigating Latent Knowledge Gaps in Narrative Drafting via Mixed-Initiative Scaffolding

supplement.where: Supplemental material referred to in the text; no URL given
supplement.holds: Full study instruments, scale items, deception experiment details, and full statistical analysis details (p. 8, Sections 5.5.3 and 5.5.4)

paper_design_summary: Nine fiction writers (5 professionals, 4 hobbyists) participated in formative artifact-driven interviews (PDF p. 4, Section 3; p. 14, Table 1). In a remote, moderated within-person study, 12 writers (8 hobbyists, 4 online novelists) each produced two 250-to-400-word story continuations in 30-minute sessions using VeriForge and a strengthened generative-AI baseline, with domain and condition order counterbalanced but the allocation method unreported (pp. 7-8, Sections 5-5.4). Two external published authors blindly rated the writing-session snippets on three 7-point domain-grounding dimensions, also combined into a composite; word count, self-reported scales, and one-week knowledge recall were also reported (p. 8, Sections 5.5.1-5.5.3; p. 10, Sections 6.2 and 6.4).

studies.label: Within-subjects user study (story continuation, VeriForge vs. baseline)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Order of the two system conditions (VeriForge vs. strengthened baseline) and of the two writing domains; every participant used both systems
assignment.quote: We counterbalanced the order of both writing domains and system conditions across participants to minimize learning effects.
assignment.prereg_locator: Full text, including Appendices A-C (p. 14), contains no preregistration statement; ethics approval is reported on p. 7, Section 5.

arms.name: VeriForge
arms.description: Mixed-initiative writing system: proactive inline highlighting of knowledge gaps, dual-stream query panel with source-anchored Knowledge Cards, spatial Knowledge Canvas with AI-reasoned connections, on a graph-based RAG backend

arms.name: Baseline
arms.description: Strengthened baseline: text editor, Miro-like canvas, and conversational query panel in one interface, connected to the same graph-based retrieval backend, without VeriForge's proactive and card mechanisms

participants.exclusions: No person-level exclusions are stated. Zero paired differences were excluded separately from each Wilcoxon signed-rank test; tied absolute differences received average ranks. Test-specific effective sample sizes (N_eff) are not printed and remain unknown; the main count of 12 people is not assumed to be the effective sample for every rank test (PDF p. 8, Section 5.5.4).
participants.who: 8 creative writing hobbyists and 4 online novelists recruited through local and online writing communities, screened for little prior knowledge of the two martial-arts domains; 10 of 12 had used AI writing tools. Each participant is in both arms. An earlier pilot of MS Word + ChatGPT + Miro involved three participants; those sessions were treated as formative, but whether those individuals also participated in the main user study is not stated (PDF p. 7, Sections 5.1-5.2).
participants.quote: We recruited 12 participants (8 creative writing hobbyists and 4 online novelists) through local and online writing communities.
participants.locator: p. 7, Section 5.2; p. 10, Section 6.4 ("10 of 12 pairs"); p. 14, Table 2 (N = 12)

ai_tool.name_model: VeriForge (Qwen3.5-Flash API for text generation and entity extraction, BAAI/bge-m3 embeddings, Neo4j graph RAG); baseline uses the same backend
ai_tool.how_used: System flags potential domain-knowledge gaps in the author's draft and supplies source-anchored facts (Knowledge Cards, conversational answers, canvas nodes); it does not write prose. Baseline offers only reactive conversational querying on the same retrieval backend.

task.description: Constrained story continuation: draft a narrative scene of about 250 to 400 words that depends on historical domain detail (Medieval European martial arts or Republican-era Chinese martial arts), one domain per condition

outcomes.name: Expert rating: perceived authorial domain competence
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Perceived authorial domain competence: whether the passage creates a convincing illusion that the author understands the domain. Two published authors external to the participant sample blindly rated anonymized writing-session story snippets on 7-point Likert scales; their scores were averaged for analysis. These dimensions assess verisimilitude/domain grounding. Across the three dimensions, single-rater absolute-agreement ICC(A,1) = 0.53-0.59 (PDF p. 8, Section 5.5.3; p. 14, Appendix C). These are the immediate writing-session artifacts, not the delayed recall paragraphs (p. 8, Sections 5.3-5.5.3). Tests use two-sided paired Wilcoxon signed ranks with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across the three expert dimensions; the reported r = |Z|/sqrt(N_eff) is a Wilcoxon effect size, not a standardized mean difference. Test-specific N_eff is not printed (PDF p. 8, Section 5.5.4).

contrasts.reported: VeriForge M = 4.58 vs. baseline M = 3.58; W = 2.5, p = .005, q = .015, r = .818 (two-sided paired Wilcoxon, BH-FDR corrected; 7-point scale, mean of two blind published-author raters)

outcomes.name: Expert rating: natural integration of domain details
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Natural integration of domain details: whether specialized details are woven organically into the narrative rather than inserted as encyclopedia entries. Two published authors external to the participant sample blindly rated anonymized writing-session story snippets on 7-point Likert scales; their scores were averaged for analysis. These dimensions assess verisimilitude/domain grounding. Across the three dimensions, single-rater absolute-agreement ICC(A,1) = 0.53-0.59 (PDF p. 8, Section 5.5.3; p. 14, Appendix C). These are the immediate writing-session artifacts, not the delayed recall paragraphs (p. 8, Sections 5.3-5.5.3). Tests use two-sided paired Wilcoxon signed ranks with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across the three expert dimensions; the reported r = |Z|/sqrt(N_eff) is a Wilcoxon effect size, not a standardized mean difference. Test-specific N_eff is not printed (PDF p. 8, Section 5.5.4).

contrasts.reported: VeriForge M = 4.92 vs. baseline M = 4.25; p = .045, q = .065, r = .617 (did not survive FDR correction)

contrasts.reported: VeriForge M = 4.17 vs. baseline M = 3.54; p = .065, q = .065, r = .536 (did not survive FDR correction).

outcomes.name: Expert rating: composite domain grounding
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Composite combining the three expert verisimilitude/domain-grounding dimensions. Two published authors external to the participant sample blindly rated anonymized writing-session story snippets on 7-point Likert scales; their scores were averaged for analysis. These dimensions assess verisimilitude/domain grounding. Across the three dimensions, single-rater absolute-agreement ICC(A,1) = 0.53-0.59 (PDF p. 8, Section 5.5.3; p. 14, Appendix C). These are the immediate writing-session artifacts, not the delayed recall paragraphs (p. 8, Sections 5.3-5.5.3). The composite test is a two-sided paired Wilcoxon test reported without FDR correction (PDF p. 10, Section 6.4; p. 9, Figure 5 caption). The reported r = |Z|/sqrt(N_eff) is a Wilcoxon effect size, not a standardized mean difference; test-specific N_eff is not printed (p. 8, Section 5.5.4).

contrasts.reported: VeriForge M = 4.56 vs. baseline M = 3.79; p = .005, r = .770; 10 of 12 pairs favoring VeriForge. Two-sided paired Wilcoxon composite test, uncorrected.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 10, Section 6.4; p. 9, Figure 5 (right panel and caption); p. 8, Section 5.5.4.

outcomes.name: Story word count
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Number of words in the writing-session story snippet, coded as elaboration because the codebook includes output length. The paper does not state how words were counted, so the scoring method is left null. The paper reports no numerical word-count SD, test statistic, or effect size (PDF p. 10, Section 6.4). The statistical methods specify paired Wilcoxon tests with zero differences excluded; test-specific N_eff is not printed (p. 8, Section 5.5.4).

contrasts.reported: VeriForge M = 285.83 words vs. baseline M = 258.25 words; p = .532.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 10, Section 6.4; p. 8, Sections 5.3-5.4 (writing-session artifacts).

studies.label: Formative artifact-driven interviews with fiction writers

assignment.what_was_assigned: No experimental AI-assistance assignment: interviews about existing writing practices and retrospective walkthroughs of participants' own research-intensive passages.
assignment.quote: we conducted artifact-driven interviews with 9 fiction writers (5 professionals, 4 hobbyists)
assignment.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 3; p. 14, Appendix A, Table 1. Assignment structure is not applicable to these qualitative interviews.
assignment.prereg_locator: Full text, including p. 4, Section 3 and p. 14, Appendices A-C; no preregistration statement.

participants.who: 9 fiction writers (5 professionals, 4 hobbyists) recruited through social media platforms. This is the formative interview sample; its count is not added to the main user-study sample. Overlap with the main user-study or pilot participants is not stated.
participants.quote: we conducted artifact-driven interviews with 9 fiction writers (5 professionals, 4 hobbyists)
participants.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 3; p. 14, Appendix A, Table 1.

ai_tool.how_used: No experimental AI-assistance condition. Researchers fact-checked submitted passages using domain references and LLM-assisted verification; the model used for this verification is not stated (PDF p. 4, Section 3).

task.description: Artifact-driven interviews on writing and research practices, followed by retrospective walkthroughs of participants' own research-intensive chapters or passages; qualitative thematic analysis, with no quantitative creativity contrast (PDF p. 4, Section 3).

eligibility.reason: The main within-person comparison analyzed 12 people, below the 50-person threshold (PDF p. 7, Section 5.2; p. 10, Section 6.4; p. 14, Table 2). Condition and domain order were counterbalanced, but random allocation of order is not stated, so neither a randomized nor an explicitly non-random assignment is established (p. 7, Section 5.1). Both arms use a generative-AI backend, making this an AI-configuration comparison (p. 7, Section 5.1; p. 14, Table 3). Criterion 3 is met under the codebook's elaboration definition, which includes output length: story word count is an output-scored result (p. 10, Section 6.4; creativity-codebook.md, Section 6). The expert ratings measure domain grounding/verisimilitude rather than overall creativity, and CSI is self-reported (p. 8, Sections 5.5.1 and 5.5.3). The separate 9-writer formative interview study reports no experimental AI assignment or quantitative creativity contrast (p. 4, Section 3; p. 14, Table 1). Neither sample meets core eligibility, and the paper supplies no qualifying AI-versus-human, observational-output, or synthesis context evidence.

one_line_finding: With 12 writers in a within-subjects comparison, blind expert ratings of story snippets were higher with VeriForge than with the baseline on perceived domain competence (4.58 vs. 3.58, p = .005, q = .015), with smaller uncorrected-significant or non-significant gains on natural integration (4.92 vs. 4.25) and specificity (4.17 vs. 3.54) (p. 10, Section 6.4; p. 9, Figure 5).
notes: The full markdown conversion and all 14 PDF pages, including Appendices A-C, were read; Figure 5's expert-rating means were also checked visually. Numerical SDs for the expert ratings are not printed in that panel, so none were estimated from its error bars. Reported standardized_effect entries refer to Wilcoxon r = |Z|/sqrt(N_eff), not standardized mean differences; no effect sizes were computed. Test-specific effective sample sizes after zero-difference exclusions are not printed (PDF p. 8, Section 5.5.4). The three-person tool-chain pilot is documented as formative development in Section 5.1; participant overlap is not stated and its count is not added to either study. Formative assignment.structure is null because experimental allocation does not apply; the researcher verification model and the word-count scoring method are unreported and left null. Self-reported creativity support and delayed knowledge recall are not coded as creativity/diversity outcomes.
